## Summary

I rebuilt the ISIS-style SANS instrument exactly per the specification: an `ISIS_moderator` (Face="E2", energy-windowed by `Lmin`/`Lmax`) feeding a 10-element curved `Guide_gravity` bender (each 0.3245 m, rotated +0.13–0.1375° increments) into two `PSD_monitor`/`L_monitor` diagnostic pairs, a `Slit` collimation entrance, four straight `Guide_gravity` guide sections (4×1.985 m), then the SANS collimation train: `aperture1` (rect, A1w×A1h), `S6slit` (circular radius S6), `APERTURE2` (circular radius A2, positioned at L1 downstream of aperture1), ending in a wavelength and PSD monitor pair at the sample position. All 25 components validated and ran successfully with gravity enabled (appropriate given λ up to 14 Å and ~20 m total flight path).

**Run conditions:** `ncount = 2×10⁷`, `seed = 12345`, `gravity = true`, parameters L1=3.926, A1w=0.030, A1h=0.02, S6=0.006, A2=0.006, Lmin=1, Lmax=14. All monitors clear the 1000-event statistics floor (min 501,911 events; rel. err ≤ 0.15%), so every quoted number below is trustworthy.

### Integrated intensity per monitor (I ± err [n/s], events N)

| Monitor | Type | Position (z, m) | I ± err [n/s] | N (events) | rel. err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lmon1 | L_monitor (λ) | 3.698 | 2.57527×10⁸ ± 5.76×10⁴ | 2.00×10⁷ | 0.02% |
| psd1 | PSD_monitor | 3.699 | 2.57527×10⁸ ± 5.76×10⁴ | 2.00×10⁷ | 0.02% |
| lmonb | L_monitor (λ, after bender) | 6.951 | 1.2565×10⁸ ± 3.90×10⁴ | 1.499×10⁷ | 0.03% |
| psd2 | PSD_monitor (after bender) | 6.952 | 1.2565×10⁸ ± 3.90×10⁴ | 1.499×10⁷ | 0.03% |
| psd3 | PSD_monitor (after straight guides) | 15.233 | 9.07537×10⁷ ± 3.32×10⁴ | 1.241×10⁷ | 0.04% |
| lmonitor2 | L_monitor (after A1) | 17.884 | 4.68511×10⁷ ± 2.39×10⁴ | 5.120×10⁶ | 0.05% |
| lmon2 | L_monitor (at sample, after A2) | 19.444 | 5.46117×10⁶ ± 8.18×10³ | 5.019×10⁵ | 0.15% |
| psd4 | PSD_monitor (at sample, after A2) | 19.445 | 5.46117×10⁶ ± 8.18×10³ | 5.019×10⁵ | 0.15% |

### Transmission chain sanity check
- Source → after bender (psd1→psd2): ×0.49 (bender losses, expected for m=1/3 mirrors + 9-channel splitting).
- After bender → after 4 straight guides (psd2→psd3): ×0.72 (guide transmission losses over ~8 m, reasonable).
- After guide → after A1 (30×20 mm rectangular aperture) (psd3→lmonitor2): ×0.52 (aperture clips wide beam tails, expected — aperture matches source-focus width but guide beam divergence exceeds it slightly).
- After A1 → after A2 (6 mm radius pinhole) (lmonitor2→lmon2): ×0.117, consistent with going from a 30×20mm aperture down to a Ø12mm circular pinhole (geometric area ratio ≈ (π·6²)/(30·20/... ) — a ~10× drop from a large rectangular aperture to a small circular pinhole is expected collimation loss, not a bug).
- Beam centers (X0, Y0) stay within ~mm of axis at every stage (small drift from bender curvature/gravity, as expected for a curved cold-neutron guide).

No unexplained (>10×, unphysical) drops were observed at any stage; the intensity decreases track the known geometric/optical loss mechanisms (bender reflectivity, guide transmission, and aperture stopping-down from 30×20 mm → Ø6 mm circular pinholes), consistent with a working SANS collimation train. The final sample-position flux is **5.46×10⁶ ± 8.2×10³ n/s** through the 6 mm-radius aperture2, with a λ-band centered near 4.3 Å (broadened tail toward 14 Å) as expected from the E2 moderator face windowed to Lmin=1–Lmax=14 Å.

## Summary

I rebuilt the ISIS-style SANS instrument exactly per the specification: an `ISIS_moderator` (Face="E2", energy-windowed by `Lmin`/`Lmax`) feeding a 10-element curved `Guide_gravity` bender (each 0.3245 m, rotated +0.13–0.1375° increments) into two `PSD_monitor`/`L_monitor` diagnostic pairs, a `Slit` collimation entrance, four straight `Guide_gravity` guide sections (4×1.985 m), then the SANS collimation train: `aperture1` (rect, A1w×A1h), `S6slit` (circular radius S6), `APERTURE2` (circular radius A2, positioned at L1 downstream of aperture1), ending in a wavelength and PSD monitor pair at the sample position. All 25 components validated and ran successfully with gravity enabled (appropriate given λ up to 14 Å and ~20 m total flight path).

**Run conditions:** `ncount = 2×10⁷`, `seed = 12345`, `gravity = true`, parameters L1=3.926, A1w=0.030, A1h=0.02, S6=0.006, A2=0.006, Lmin=1, Lmax=14. All monitors clear the 1000-event statistics floor (min 501,911 events; rel. err ≤ 0.15%), so every quoted number below is trustworthy.

### Integrated intensity per monitor (I ± err [n/s], events N)

| Monitor | Type | Position (z, m) | I ± err [n/s] | N (events) | rel. err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lmon1 | L_monitor (λ) | 3.698 | 2.57527×10⁸ ± 5.76×10⁴ | 2.00×10⁷ | 0.02% |
| psd1 | PSD_monitor | 3.699 | 2.57527×10⁸ ± 5.76×10⁴ | 2.00×10⁷ | 0.02% |
| lmonb | L_monitor (λ, after bender) | 6.951 | 1.2565×10⁸ ± 3.90×10⁴ | 1.499×10⁷ | 0.03% |
| psd2 | PSD_monitor (after bender) | 6.952 | 1.2565×10⁸ ± 3.90×10⁴ | 1.499×10⁷ | 0.03% |
| psd3 | PSD_monitor (after straight guides) | 15.233 | 9.07537×10⁷ ± 3.32×10⁴ | 1.241×10⁷ | 0.04% |
| lmonitor2 | L_monitor (after A1) | 17.884 | 4.68511×10⁷ ± 2.39×10⁴ | 5.120×10⁶ | 0.05% |
| lmon2 | L_monitor (at sample, after A2) | 19.444 | 5.46117×10⁶ ± 8.18×10³ | 5.019×10⁵ | 0.15% |
| psd4 | PSD_monitor (at sample, after A2) | 19.445 | 5.46117×10⁶ ± 8.18×10³ | 5.019×10⁵ | 0.15% |

### Transmission chain sanity check
- Source → after bender (psd1→psd2): ×0.49 (bender losses, expected for m=1/3 mirrors + 9-channel splitting).
- After bender → after 4 straight guides (psd2→psd3): ×0.72 (guide transmission losses over ~8 m, reasonable).
- After guide → after A1 (30×20 mm rectangular aperture) (psd3→lmonitor2): ×0.52 (aperture clips wide beam tails, expected — aperture matches source-focus width but guide beam divergence exceeds it slightly).
- After A1 → after A2 (6 mm radius pinhole) (lmonitor2→lmon2): ×0.117, consistent with going from a 30×20mm aperture down to a Ø12mm circular pinhole (geometric area ratio ≈ (π·6²)/(30·20/... ) — a ~10× drop from a large rectangular aperture to a small circular pinhole is expected collimation loss, not a bug).
- Beam centers (X0, Y0) stay within ~mm of axis at every stage (small drift from bender curvature/gravity, as expected for a curved cold-neutron guide).

No unexplained (>10×, unphysical) drops were observed at any stage; the intensity decreases track the known geometric/optical loss mechanisms (bender reflectivity, guide transmission, and aperture stopping-down from 30×20 mm → Ø6 mm circular pinholes), consistent with a working SANS collimation train. The final sample-position flux is **5.46×10⁶ ± 8.2×10³ n/s** through the 6 mm-radius aperture2, with a λ-band centered near 4.3 Å (broadened tail toward 14 Å) as expected from the E2 moderator face windowed to Lmin=1–Lmax=14 Å.
